prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour’s 2010 manifesto sets out a progressive plan for a future fair for all: using active, reforming government to secure the recovery, protect frontline services, and widen opportunity, while demanding responsibility from the top and empowering citizens to shape better services.

- Securing recovery with fairness: No premature cuts that risk recession; more than halving the deficit by 2014 through growth, tough efficiency savings, and fair tax measures (bank bonus tax, reduced pension relief for the highest earners, 50p top rate, 1p NIC next year with protection for low earners). Reform finance (stronger capital, “living wills,” global levy), promote competition and long‑termism (two‑thirds shareholder threshold on takeovers), and back enterprise with UK Finance for Growth, R&D credits, capital allowances, a Green Investment Bank and nationwide broadband. Build high-speed rail, modern railways, and electric vehicle infrastructure.

- Work, wages, skills, homes: Restore full employment with job guarantees (Future Jobs Fund; mandatory jobs after two years unemployed), make work pay (minimum wage rising at least with average earnings; £40 “Better Off in Work” guarantee), expand advanced apprenticeships and Skills Accounts. Help first‑time buyers (no stamp duty up to £250,000 for two years, paid for by 5% on £1m+ homes), build affordable and council homes, and curb predatory lending with a People’s Bank at the Post Office and a universal banking obligation.

- Excellent, personal public services: Protect frontline spending on Sure Start/childcare, schools, NHS and policing; drive reform so citizens have enforceable guarantees and real choice. In schools, a 3Rs guarantee with one‑to‑one tuition; stronger leadership via takeovers/mergers where standards lag; parental triggers; fair admissions and a local pupil premium; staying in learning to 18 and major growth in apprenticeships and higher education. In the NHS, legally binding rights (18‑week treatment or NHS‑funded private care; one‑week cancer test results; GP access evenings/weekends), more prevention and mental health therapy, choice of any qualified provider at NHS cost, and more care at home. Create a National Care Service (free home care for highest needs now; cap on residential care costs after two years; path to comprehensive, free adult care after 2015).

- Stronger families and fairness in later life: Support every family (not just the married) with a new Toddler Tax Credit, a flexible “Father’s Month,” extended flexible working and an end to default retirement at 65. Restore the earnings link for the Basic State Pension in 2012 and auto‑enrol ten million people into Personal Pension Accounts.

- Safe, cohesive communities and controlled migration: Maintain police and PCSO numbers; fast, visible action on anti‑social behaviour (injunction rights for repeat victims; expanded Community Payback). Use DNA/CCTV responsibly to cut crime. Control immigration through a points‑based system (no unskilled migration from outside the EU), tougher English requirements, and a path to earned citizenship.

- Green growth and quality of life: Target around 40% low‑carbon electricity by 2020 (renewables, nuclear, clean coal/CCS), 400,000 green jobs by 2015, pay‑as‑you‑save home upgrades, smart meters, warmer social and private rented homes, and a move toward zero waste. Protect nature (Green Belt, new habitat networks, more forests) and support thriving rural communities.

- A new, accountable politics: Clean up Parliament (independent regulation, recall for misconduct, lobbyist register, ban MPs working for lobbying firms), empower citizens and local government, open up public data, and hold referenda on AV for Commons and an elected Second Chamber, with fixed‑term Parliaments and a free vote on votes at 16 after better citizenship education.

- A confident Britain abroad: Back our forces (Strategic Defence Review, modern kit, Forces Charter), pursue security and development in Afghanistan to enable Afghan lead, keep the nuclear deterrent while pressing global disarmament, lead in a reformed EU, enshrine 0.7% aid in law, drive the MDGs, and reform global institutions to meet 21st‑century challenges.
